description: Development fixture for the code-review benchmark. Deliberately NOT representative — chosen to exercise the runner across languages, sizes and merge strategies while the harness is built. The curated 15-20 PR set is separate.

prs.notes: Dependabot lockfile bump (fast-uri 3.1.4 -> 3.1.5, indirect dep). Correct answer is zero findings. Only mcp/package-lock.json changed, which matches none of the funnel's rule-relevant extensions or named files, so the pr-review command's Step 4 early exit fires. Note this repo's origin remote is upstream florianbuetow/tts-mcp; the PR lives on the fork remote.

Two real defects documented at the time: a latent nil-poster dereference in pkg/steps_review.go (tryDismissHallucinated called DismissCurrentReview with no nil guard), and a typed-nil trap where a nil concrete pointer inside an interface is non-nil, so guards fall through while a BeNil() assertion still passes. The second was explicitly recorded as one no unit test would have caught, making it a judgment-tier target rather than a mechanical one.

21 files, 31 lines total. Probes the false-positive class where a minimal diff in debt-heavy files draws findings from surrounding unchanged code. Expect diff-scoping of the funnel to matter more here than rule coverage.

CommonJS JavaScript to CommonJS TypeScript conversion. Largest entry and the only squash merge, so it is the regression case for merge-strategy handling: head_sha equals merge_sha because a squash commit has one parent. Exercises the 24 node rules.
Vulnerability and secret scanning gates. Exercises the 13 python rules.
